crawls_needed.label: ESTIMATE
crawls_needed.note: newest first; CC-NEWS (all months) is added first when included

gap_fill_candidates.name: Internet Archive (Wayback Machine + collections)
gap_fill_candidates.published_as: over 210 PB of unique data (2025 storage growth slide)
gap_fill_candidates.access: NOT an open bulk-download dataset. Wayback WARCs are generally not publicly downloadable in bulk; HPLT obtained 3.7 PB only via a research partnership. Requires an agreement with the Internet Archive; many collections are copyrighted media.

gap_fill_candidates.name: NOAA Open Data Dissemination (NODD) - weather/climate/satellite
gap_fill_candidates.published_as: more than 24 PB (PiB) as of September 2022
gap_fill_candidates.source: https://exa.ai/library/publication/mw23mc20x9g  (paper: 'NOAA Open Data Dissemination: Petabyte-scale Earth system data in the cloud'); registry: https://registry.opendata.aws/collab/noaa/
gap_fill_candidates.access: Open, free (AWS/Azure/GCP buckets). Scientific gridded/satellite data - NOT web text; only useful for a multimodal/scientific model. Some products now have 90-day rolling retention.

gap_fill_candidates.name: Software Heritage archive (source code)
gap_fill_candidates.published_as: object storage about 3.6 PB, +~750 TB/year (Dec 2025 estimate)
gap_fill_candidates.access: Bulk copy only via an official mirror agreement or their published dataset exports; files carry their own (mixed) open-source licences - licence filtering required. 26-28 billion small files.

gap_fill_candidates.name: Wikimedia Commons (freely licensed media)
gap_fill_candidates.published_as: exceeded 1 PiB of current, undeleted files on 19 Aug 2026
gap_fill_candidates.access: Open licences (CC-BY/CC-BY-SA/PD) per file - attribution metadata must be kept. Images/video/audio; bulk via Wikimedia dumps/mirrors, polite rate limits.

gap_fill_candidates.name: HPLT v2 monolingual text (Internet Archive + Common Crawl derived)
gap_fill_candidates.published_as: 21 TB deduplicated / 15 TB cleaned, 193 languages, ~7.6T words
gap_fill_candidates.access: Open download (wget map files). Partly overlaps Common Crawl (0.8 PB of its 4.5 PB input was CC); the IA part (3.7 PB input) is new.

gap_fill_candidates.name: FineWeb (Hugging Face) - filtered Common Crawl text
gap_fill_candidates.access: Open (ODC-By). Already-processed subset OF Common Crawl - adds no new raw volume, but saves compute.

gap_fill_math.note: PUBLISHED sizes, not measured; raw bytes are not training value - media/scientific bytes yield little or no LM text.

network.common_crawl_location: AWS S3 bucket s3://commoncrawl in us-east-1 (N. Virginia), HTTPS mirror https://data.commoncrawl.org/ (source: https://commoncrawl.org/get-started)
egress_notes: Common Crawl is hosted by the AWS Open Data Sponsorship program; HTTPS download is free to the requester (commoncrawl.org/get-started). Azure charges $0 for data transfer IN (price API above).

Cross-cloud pulls at this scale are throttled: our own measurement run got HTTP 403/503 rate-limit responses at only 4-8 concurrent HEAD requests. Multi-Gbps sustained pulls need coordination with Common Crawl.

Common Crawl recommends processing IN AWS us-east-1 next to the data. Doing extraction there and shipping only the text (~9.3% of WARC bytes) to Azure cuts transfer ~11x; AWS egress on that text is billed by AWS (AWS price NOT fetched here - check https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/pricing/on-demand/#Data_Transfer).
Azure East US is also in Virginia, so latency to us-east-1 is low, but it is still internet/cross-cloud traffic.

blockers: All measured Common Crawl data (12.254 PB) is BELOW the 29.000 PB target; shortfall 16.746 PB. Open TEXT data cannot close this gap; only media/scientific archives or partnership data (Internet Archive) are that large.
Default Azure limits: 5 PiB/storage account, 250 accounts/region, 60 Gbps ingress/account, low default Batch/Spot vCPU quota -> support requests needed before any real run.
Common Crawl rate limiting (observed 403/503) caps cross-cloud throughput; plan for AWS-side extraction or a CC agreement.
Spot capacity for thousands of vCPUs in one region is not guaranteed; spread across regions/VM sizes.
Licensing: Common Crawl ToU allows use, but page copyrights remain with owners - licence/robots/opt-out filtering is required.
